chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the one who drinks (wine), so he said: As for a man who had a slip (occasional drinking) from him, then I would excuse him; and as for another who makes it a habit, then I would severely punish him, because he considers all prohibitions permissible, and if people were left with that, they would become corrupt.

key_terms.يُدْمِنُ: He makes it a habit / is addicted

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for occasional versus habitual wine drinkers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a jurisprudential distinction between a single slip (zallat) and habitual intoxication (idmān), prescribing light correction for the former and severe punishment for the latter. The rationale is that habitual drinkers normalize the haram, leading to a broader moral decay where all prohibitions become permissible, thereby causing societal corruption if unchecked. This reflects the Shia principle of proportionality in punishment (taʿzīr) based on the depth of the sinner's disregard for divine law.
